caveats: asset values are as of the end of the reporting year; liabilities are the highest amount owed during it
amounts are the disclosed bands; no midpoint is stored
excludes: personal residences and non-rental second or vacation homes (not reported on Schedule A), and mortgages or home-equity loans on them (reported by Members on Schedule D, but left out of this figure)
federal retirement benefits including the Thrift Savings Plan
non-interest-bearing checking and savings deposits; personal property (cars, art, jewellery, furniture)
debts owed to the filer by close relatives or without interest; term life insurance; HSA/FSA cash
assets that were not reported because their value was $1,000 or less and income $200 or less; liabilities of $10,000 or less
the spouse's assets when separated; underlying assets of excepted and qualified blind trusts
assets held solely by a spouse or dependent child reported as 'Spouse/DC over $1,000,000' (open-ended)
earned income, gifts, positions and agreements (Schedules C, E-J are not in the source dataset)
net_worth_definition.name: disclosed net worth range
net_worth_definition.rule: low = sum of asset lows - sum of liability highs; high = sum of asset highs - sum of liability lows. Unvalued assets add 0 to low (a value is never negative) and make high null; high_valued is the same figure over valued assets only. An open-ended band ("Over $X") makes high null: the figure is then 'at least' low. Liabilities secured by a personal residence are listed but not subtracted, because the residence itself is not reported.
